title: We’re running out of reasons to ignore AI safety
excerpt: In the aftermath of OpenAI’s attack on Hugging Face, experts say it’s time for everyone to take security far more seriously.
content_html:
Earlier this month, OpenAI gave several of its AI models a task: complete a test designed to measure their cybersecurity capabilities. It put the systems in a sandboxed environment without an internet connection and set them off to work.

What happened next is almost laughably silly — but also, as Adam Gleave, cofounder and CEO of AI safety organization FAR.AI, put it, “a visceral example of how misaligned AI could cause harm.” According to OpenAI, the models escaped the sandbox meant to contain them, moved through the company’s internal systems, found a route to the internet, and then started looking for a way into Hugging Face. And why was the agent looking for a way into Hugging Face? They had apparently reasoned that the developer platform might store the answers to the cyber benchmark and that getting them would be a great way to get a high score.

The incident is “a visceral example of how misaligned AI could cause harm.”

In other words, OpenAI’s agent broke out of a supposedly secure environment, traipsed through the company’s systems, got online, and compromised another company’s systems — all to cheat on a test of no particular importance.

This appears to be the first well-documented incident of its kind, or at least the first on this scale. It was both a clear example of a system pursuing a goal in an unintended way and a demonstration that frontier models are now powerful enough for that behavior to have real-world consequences.

The hack was an example of what the AI safety community calls “specification gaming,” a behavior also known as reward hacking, said Fazl Barez, an AI safety researcher at the University of Oxford. In plain English, it means “the model doing what you asked rather than what you meant,” Fazl said. It satisfies the literal terms of a task while violating the obvious intent and has been documented across many AI systems. Some researchers worry that as systems become more capable, this could produce increasingly misaligned systems, which pursue goals in ways their creators did not intend (like turning everyone into paper clips).

“Nothing in that chain is exotic in isolation,” Fazl said. A competent human tester would be able to do all of this, he added. “What is new is that the model did not stop. Older models would likely have hit some barrier and gone back to the user, he said, but this agent just “treated the barrier as part of the problem it had been asked to solve.”

OpenAI described it as “an unprecedented cyber incident,” that “marks an important moment for AI safety.” Hugging Face cofounder Thomas Wolf said it was a “wake-up call” for the industry. But this is not one of the four horsemen of the AI apocalypse. As cyber incidents go, experts told The Verge it was pretty mundane. Nothing the agent did required superhuman abilities. Moreover, frontier systems like GPT-5.6 Sol and Anthropic’s Mythos are known to be capable coders, are already thought to have been misused numerous times, and AI tools already allow hackers to scale up and refine attacks on a massive scale.

Could it be hype? The industry has spent months amplifying claims about the dangerous capabilities of its top models, particularly when it comes to cybersecurity. It is the stated reason why companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have withheld their most capable models from the general public and partly why the Trump administration hurriedly moved to apply export controls to them.

If this is hype, however, it has not gone entirely in OpenAI’s favor. In the days since, the attack has produced a rare moment of unity across much of the US tech industry about the importance of open-weight AI systems and the need to take AI security more seriously. These concerns were underscored further by the release of Kimi K3, a highly capable open-weight model from China. A broad coalition of companies including Nvidia, Microsoft, and SpaceX argued that the incident showed why defenders need access to the most capable tools available, rather than being forced to rely on proprietary providers whose built-in safeguards can limit their effectiveness in high-stakes security work. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google were notably absent from the coalition’s founding membership.

“Anyone who’s been paying attention has noted that capabilities are only going in one direction.”

OpenAI’s account of the incident undeniably fits a broader industry narrative about the dangerous capabilities of frontier models. Even so, several details make the incident difficult to dismiss as merely self-serving. Foremost, it is an example of a problem the AI industry has warned about for years — and one OpenAI could have reasonably been expected to anticipate. The episode also handed an unexpected boost to a major Chinese competitor, whose model played a prominent role in containing the breach, while exposing OpenAI to significant legal, regulatory, and reputational scrutiny. That Hugging Face appears keen to work with OpenAI and, publicly at least, has remained fairly relaxed about the whole thing may have limited the fallout. Most of the experts The Verge spoke to similarly cautioned against reducing the incident to hype.

“It’s a pretty useful warning shot in terms of demonstrating both unintended consequences and just how capable these models are,” said Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh, a professor at Cambridge University’s Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence. “Anyone who’s been paying attention has noted that capabilities are only going in one direction, and that is improving significantly over time in a way that I think is perhaps less obvious to the everyday user of something like ChatGPT.”

Still, it would be wrong to interpret this warning as a sign AI systems are about to slip human control, or that containing them is impossible, says Lin Li, an AI safety researcher at the University of Oxford. “The better lesson is that safety has to move from evaluating isolated actions to evaluating whole action sequences, environments, and operational controls,” Li says.

A crucial next step is for AI labs to be investing more heavily in securing their own systems. “There’s a clear need for AI companies to beef up the security of their internal deployments,” Gleave said, likening the current practice of responding to reward hacking incidents as they arise to a game of whack-a-mole that is becoming less and less tenable as stakes rise. Alan Chan, a research fellow at tech policy research center GovAI, said companies should consider airgapping their machines — physically isolating them from the internet and other networks — “until they’re sure about the model’s capabilities.” Intensifying work on alignment, which ensures systems reliably follow human intentions, and more rigorous testing “to surface these issues before putting models in environments where they have the tools to be able to do these things,” would also be good ideas, he said.

As model capabilities increase, experts warn that we can’t rely on technical safeguards alone. Peter Wallich, a former UK AI Security Institute official, said the incident illustrated the limits of relying on sandboxing agents and defensive security measures alone: “Two multibillion dollar companies just tried this approach and — self-evidently, based on their own reporting — failed.”

One of the biggest priorities should be ensuring outsiders can see what is happening inside frontier AI labs. “We only know about this incident because OpenAI chose to tell us,” said Patrick Levermore, at the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, a British think tank. “A good safety regime shouldn’t depend on voluntary disclosure.” The need is especially acute when, as Wallich noted, the conduct in question “would be a crime if done by a human.” Ó hÉigeartaigh pointed to whistleblower protections, third-party audits, and mandatory reporting of serious incidents as possible ways to provide that visibility, stressing that oversight must span the entire development lifecycle rather than begin only once products reach the market. OpenAI said that one of the models being tested has not been released yet.

“A good safety regime shouldn’t depend on voluntary disclosure.”

Lots of this presumes the companies themselves know what’s happening inside their systems. In this case, reports suggest OpenAI was unaware its own agent was behind the dayslong cyber campaign at Hugging Face and did not notice until well after the threat had been contained and the FBI contacted. There are still many details about the hack that are unknown or have not been made public. In an update on social media, OpenAI said it is conducting a review and will publish a technical report of its findings “in the coming weeks.”

Whether the warnings raised by the Hugging Face incident produce any lasting change, or join the long list of warnings the tech industry absorbs without meaningfully altering course, remains uncertain. For now, at least, it does appear to have alarmed industry insiders and pushed US lawmakers to consider new rules before the next containment failure. The incident also added to a broader sense of unease over the speed of AI development, which deepened in the days that followed as employees from leading US labs signed a statement backing coordinated global governance — including a potential slowdown in frontier AI development.

The prevailing view of those The Verge spoke to was that this hack marked the start of a new class of risk, even if its significance may only become clear in hindsight. One former government AI policy expert, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to be quoted by name, described it as a “red line,” the kind of watershed moment we may later look back on as marking a new, riskier stage in our relationship with AI. They hope it will force the tech industry to take the management of frontier systems more seriously and spur governments to think more deeply about oversight before a less benign breach occurs. Their fear is that it will instead join the long list of warnings about AI’s growing capabilities that were recognized, discussed, and ultimately left unheeded.

That may prove overstated. But if this is a warning, we should consider ourselves lucky the AI agent was only trying to cheat on a test.

Correction July 29th: An earlier version of this story misspelled Alan Chan’s name.

These concerns were underscored further by the release of Kimi K3, a highly capable open-weight model from China. A broad coalition of companies including Nvidia, Microsoft, and SpaceX argued that the incident showed why defenders need access to the most capable tools available, rather than being forced to rely on proprietary providers whose built-in safeguards can limit their effectiveness in high-stakes security work. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google were notably absent from the coalition’s founding membership.

sentences.en: If this is hype, however, it has not gone entirely in OpenAI’s favor.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果这只是炒作，那么它并没有完全对 OpenAI 有利。

sentences.en: In the days since, the attack has produced a rare moment of unity across much of the US tech industry about the importance of open-weight AI systems and the need to take AI security more seriously.
sentences.zh: 在那之后的几天里，这次攻击在美国科技行业的大部分地区产生了罕见的团结时刻，让人们认识到开放式人工智能系统的重要性以及更加认真对待人工智能安全的必要性。

sentences.en: These concerns were underscored further by the release of Kimi K3, a highly capable open-weight model from China.
sentences.zh: 来自中国的高性能开放式重量模型 Kimi K3 的发布进一步凸显了这些担忧。

sentences.en: A broad coalition of companies including Nvidia, Microsoft, and SpaceX argued that the incident showed why defenders need access to the most capable tools available, rather than being forced to rely on proprietary providers whose built-in safeguards can limit their effectiveness in high-stakes security work.
sentences.zh: 包括英伟达、微软和 SpaceX 在内的一个广泛的公司联盟认为，这一事件表明，为什么防御者需要获得最强大的可用工具，而不是被迫依赖专有提供商，因为这些提供商的内置保护措施可能会限制他们在高风险安全工作中的有效性。

sentences.en: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google were notably absent from the coalition’s founding membership.
sentences.zh: OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 显然没有出现在该联盟的创始成员名单中。

blocks.html_en: “Anyone who’s been paying attention has noted that capabilities are only going in one direction.”

sentences.en: “Anyone who’s been paying attention has noted that capabilities are only going in one direction.”
sentences.zh: “任何关注的人都注意到，能力只会朝一个方向发展。”

blocks.html_en: OpenAI’s account of the incident undeniably fits a broader industry narrative about the dangerous capabilities of frontier models. Even so, several details make the incident difficult to dismiss as merely self-serving. Foremost, it is an example of a problem the AI industry has warned about for years — and one OpenAI could have reasonably been expected to anticipate. The episode also handed an unexpected boost to a major Chinese competitor, whose model played a prominent role in containing the breach, while exposing OpenAI to significant legal, regulatory, and reputational scrutiny. That Hugging Face appears keen to work with OpenAI and, publicly at least, has remained fairly relaxed about the whole thing may have limited the fallout. Most of the experts The Verge spoke to similarly cautioned against reducing the incident to hype.

sentences.en: OpenAI’s account of the incident undeniably fits a broader industry narrative about the dangerous capabilities of frontier models.
sentences.zh: 不可否认，OpenAI 对这一事件的描述符合更广泛的行业关于前沿模型危险能力的叙述。

sentences.en: Even so, several details make the incident difficult to dismiss as merely self-serving.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，一些细节使得这一事件很难被视为纯粹是为了自私而被忽视。

sentences.en: Foremost, it is an example of a problem the AI industry has warned about for years — and one OpenAI could have reasonably been expected to anticipate.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这是人工智能行业多年来一直警告的一个问题的一个例子，而 OpenAI 本来可以合理地预期它会预见到这一问题。

sentences.en: The episode also handed an unexpected boost to a major Chinese competitor, whose model played a prominent role in containing the breach, while exposing OpenAI to significant legal, regulatory, and reputational scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 这一事件还给一家主要的中国竞争对手带来了意想不到的推动，该竞争对手的模型在遏制违规行为方面发挥了重要作用，同时使 OpenAI 面临严格的法律、监管和声誉审查。

sentences.en: That Hugging Face appears keen to work with OpenAI and, publicly at least, has remained fairly relaxed about the whole thing may have limited the fallout.
sentences.zh: Hugging Face 似乎热衷于与 OpenAI 合作，并且至少在公开场合对整个事情保持相当轻松的态度，这可能限制了影响。

sentences.en: Most of the experts The Verge spoke to similarly cautioned against reducing the incident to hype.
sentences.zh: The Verge 采访的大多数专家都同样警告不要将这一事件归结为炒作。

blocks.html_en: “It’s a pretty useful warning shot in terms of demonstrating both unintended consequences and just how capable these models are,” said Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh, a professor at Cambridge University’s Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence. “Anyone who’s been paying attention has noted that capabilities are only going in one direction, and that is improving significantly over time in a way that I think is perhaps less obvious to the everyday user of something like ChatGPT.”

sentences.en: “It’s a pretty useful warning shot in terms of demonstrating both unintended consequences and just how capable these models are,” said Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh, a professor at Cambridge University’s Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence.
sentences.zh: 剑桥大学莱弗休姆未来智能中心教授 Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh 表示：“这是一个非常有用的警告，既展示了意想不到的后果，也展示了这些模型的能力。”

sentences.en: “Anyone who’s been paying attention has noted that capabilities are only going in one direction, and that is improving significantly over time in a way that I think is perhaps less obvious to the everyday user of something like ChatGPT.”
sentences.zh: “任何一直关注的人都已经注意到，这些功能只会朝一个方向发展，而且随着时间的推移，这种能力正在显着改善，我认为这种方式对于 ChatGPT 之类的日常用户来说可能不太明显。”

blocks.html_en: Still, it would be wrong to interpret this warning as a sign AI systems are about to slip human control, or that containing them is impossible, says Lin Li, an AI safety researcher at the University of Oxford. “The better lesson is that safety has to move from evaluating isolated actions to evaluating whole action sequences, environments, and operational controls,” Li says.

sentences.en: Still, it would be wrong to interpret this warning as a sign AI systems are about to slip human control, or that containing them is impossible, says Lin Li, an AI safety researcher at the University of Oxford.
sentences.zh: 牛津大学人工智能安全研究员李林表示，尽管如此，将这一警告解读为人工智能系统即将失去人类控制的迹象，或者不可能控制它们的迹象是错误的。

sentences.en: “The better lesson is that safety has to move from evaluating isolated actions to evaluating whole action sequences, environments, and operational controls,” Li says.
sentences.zh: “更好的教训是，安全必须从评估孤立的行动转向评估整个行动序列、环境和操作控制，”李说。

blocks.html_en: A crucial next step is for AI labs to be investing more heavily in securing their own systems. “There’s a clear need for AI companies to beef up the security of their internal deployments,” Gleave said, likening the current practice of responding to reward hacking incidents as they arise to a game of whack-a-mole that is becoming less and less tenable as stakes rise. Alan Chan, a research fellow at tech policy research center GovAI, said companies should consider airgapping their machines — physically isolating them from the internet and other networks — “until they’re sure about the model’s capabilities.” Intensifying work on alignment, which ensures systems reliably follow human intentions, and more rigorous testing “to surface these issues before putting models in environments where they have the tools to be able to do these things,” would also be good ideas, he said.

sentences.en: A crucial next step is for AI labs to be investing more heavily in securing their own systems.
sentences.zh: 下一步至关重要的一步是人工智能实验室加大投入以保护自己的系统。

sentences.en: “There’s a clear need for AI companies to beef up the security of their internal deployments,” Gleave said, likening the current practice of responding to reward hacking incidents as they arise to a game of whack-a-mole that is becoming less and less tenable as stakes rise.
sentences.zh: 格利夫表示：“人工智能公司显然需要加强其内部部署的安全性。”他将当前应对奖励黑客事件的做法比作打地鼠游戏，随着赌注的增加，这种游戏变得越来越站不住脚。

sentences.en: Alan Chan, a research fellow at tech policy research center GovAI, said companies should consider airgapping their machines — physically isolating them from the internet and other networks — “until they’re sure about the model’s capabilities.”
sentences.zh: 技术政策研究中心 GovAI 的研究员 Alan Chan 表示，公司应该考虑对他们的机器进行气隙保护，将它们与互联网和其他网络进行物理隔离，“直到他们确定该模型的功能。”

sentences.en: Intensifying work on alignment, which ensures systems reliably follow human intentions, and more rigorous testing “to surface these issues before putting models in environments where they have the tools to be able to do these things,” would also be good ideas, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，加强协调工作，确保系统可靠地遵循人类意图，以及进行更严格的测试，“在将模型放入拥有能够执行这些操作的工具的环境中之前，先暴露这些问题”，这也是个好主意。

blocks.html_en: As model capabilities increase, experts warn that we can’t rely on technical safeguards alone. Peter Wallich, a former UK AI Security Institute official, said the incident illustrated the limits of relying on sandboxing agents and defensive security measures alone: “Two multibillion dollar companies just tried this approach and — self-evidently, based on their own reporting — failed.”

sentences.en: As model capabilities increase, experts warn that we can’t rely on technical safeguards alone.
sentences.zh: 随着模型能力的增强，专家警告说，我们不能仅仅依赖技术保障。

sentences.en: Peter Wallich, a former UK AI Security Institute official, said the incident illustrated the limits of relying on sandboxing agents and defensive security measures alone: “Two multibillion dollar companies just tried this approach and — self-evidently, based on their own reporting — failed.”
sentences.zh: 英国人工智能安全研究所前官员 Peter Wallich 表示，这一事件说明了仅依靠沙箱代理和防御性安全措施的局限性：“两家价值数十亿美元的公司刚刚尝试了这种方法，但根据他们自己的报告，不言而喻，失败了。”

blocks.html_en: One of the biggest priorities should be ensuring outsiders can see what is happening inside frontier AI labs. “We only know about this incident because OpenAI chose to tell us,” said Patrick Levermore, at the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, a British think tank. “A good safety regime shouldn’t depend on voluntary disclosure.” The need is especially acute when, as Wallich noted, the conduct in question “would be a crime if done by a human.” Ó hÉigeartaigh pointed to whistleblower protections, third-party audits, and mandatory reporting of serious incidents as possible ways to provide that visibility, stressing that oversight must span the entire development lifecycle rather than begin only once products reach the market. OpenAI said that one of the models being tested has not been released yet.

sentences.zh: 最重要的优先事项之一应该是确保外部人员能够看到前沿人工智能实验室内部正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: “We only know about this incident because OpenAI chose to tell us,” said Patrick Levermore, at the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, a British think tank.
sentences.zh: 英国智库长期弹性中心的帕特里克·莱弗莫尔 (Patrick Levermore) 表示：“我们之所以知道这起事件，是因为 OpenAI 选择告诉我们。”

sentences.en: “A good safety regime shouldn’t depend on voluntary disclosure.”
sentences.zh: “良好的安全制度不应依赖于自愿披露。”

sentences.en: OpenAI said that one of the models being tested has not been released yet.
sentences.zh: OpenAI表示，正在测试的其中一款模型尚未发布。

sentences.zh: “良好的安全制度不应依赖于自愿披露。”

blocks.html_en: Lots of this presumes the companies themselves know what’s happening inside their systems. In this case, reports suggest OpenAI was unaware its own agent was behind the dayslong cyber campaign at Hugging Face and did not notice until well after the threat had been contained and the FBI contacted. There are still many details about the hack that are unknown or have not been made public. In an update on social media, OpenAI said it is conducting a review and will publish a technical report of its findings “in the coming weeks.”

sentences.en: Lots of this presumes the companies themselves know what’s happening inside their systems.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是假设公司本身知道他们的系统内部发生了什么。

sentences.en: In this case, reports suggest OpenAI was unaware its own agent was behind the dayslong cyber campaign at Hugging Face and did not notice until well after the threat had been contained and the FBI contacted.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，有报道称 OpenAI 并不知道自己的特工是 Hugging Face 长达数天的网络活动的幕后黑手，直到威胁得到遏制并联系 FBI 后很久才注意到。

sentences.zh: 关于此次黑客攻击仍有许多细节未知或尚未公开。

sentences.zh: OpenAI 在社交媒体上发布的最新消息表示，它正在进行审查，并将在“未来几周内”发布其调查结果的技术报告。

blocks.html_en: Whether the warnings raised by the Hugging Face incident produce any lasting change, or join the long list of warnings the tech industry absorbs without meaningfully altering course, remains uncertain. For now, at least, it does appear to have alarmed industry insiders and pushed US lawmakers to consider new rules before the next containment failure. The incident also added to a broader sense of unease over the speed of AI development, which deepened in the days that followed as employees from leading US labs signed a statement backing coordinated global governance — including a potential slowdown in frontier AI development.

sentences.en: Whether the warnings raised by the Hugging Face incident produce any lasting change, or join the long list of warnings the tech industry absorbs without meaningfully altering course, remains uncertain.
sentences.zh: 抱脸事件提出的警告是否会产生任何持久的变化，或者加入科技行业吸收的一长串警告而没有有意义地改变方向，仍然不确定。

sentences.en: For now, at least, it does appear to have alarmed industry insiders and pushed US lawmakers to consider new rules before the next containment failure.
sentences.zh: 至少就目前而言，它似乎确实引起了业内人士的警惕，并促使美国立法者在下一次遏制失败之前考虑新的规则。

sentences.en: The incident also added to a broader sense of unease over the speed of AI development, which deepened in the days that followed as employees from leading US labs signed a statement backing coordinated global governance — including a potential slowdown in frontier AI development.
sentences.zh: 这一事件还加剧了人们对人工智能发展速度的更广泛的不安情绪，在接下来的几天里，随着美国领先实验室的员工签署了一份支持协调全球治理的声明——包括前沿人工智能发展可能放缓，这种不安情绪进一步加深。

blocks.html_en: The prevailing view of those The Verge spoke to was that this hack marked the start of a new class of risk, even if its significance may only become clear in hindsight. One former government AI policy expert, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to be quoted by name, described it as a “red line,” the kind of watershed moment we may later look back on as marking a new, riskier stage in our relationship with AI. They hope it will force the tech industry to take the management of frontier systems more seriously and spur governments to think more deeply about oversight before a less benign breach occurs. Their fear is that it will instead join the long list of warnings about AI’s growing capabilities that were recognized, discussed, and ultimately left unheeded.

blocks.html_en: That may prove overstated. But if this is a warning, we should consider ourselves lucky the AI agent was only trying to cheat on a test.

blocks.html_en: • Robert Hart

sentences.en: Robert Hart
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·哈特

content_html_zh:
本月早些时候，OpenAI 给它的几个人工智能模型分配了一项任务：完成一项旨在衡量其网络安全能力的测试。 它将系统置于没有互联网连接的沙盒环境中并让它们开始工作。

接下来发生的事情几乎是可笑的愚蠢 - 但正如人工智能安全组织 FAR.AI 的联合创始人兼首席执行官 Adam Gleave 所说，“这是一个发自内心的例子，说明了人工智能的失调会如何造成伤害。” 据 OpenAI 称，这些模型逃离了旨在容纳它们的沙箱，通过公司的内部系统，找到了通往互联网的路线，然后开始寻找进入 Hugging Face 的方法。 为什么特工要寻找进入“Hugging Face”的方法？ 他们显然认为开发者平台可能会存储网络基准测试的答案，并且获得这些答案将是获得高分的好方法。

该事件是“人工智能失调如何造成伤害的一个直观例子。”

换句话说，OpenAI 的代理闯出了一个所谓的安全环境，侵入了该公司的系统，上网并破坏了另一家公司的系统——所有这些都是为了在一个并不特别重要的测试中作弊。

这似乎是同类事件中第一起有据可查的事件，或者至少是这种规模的第一起。 这既是系统以无意的方式追求目标的一个明显例子，也证明前沿模型现在已经足够强大，足以使这种行为产生现实世界的后果。

牛津大学人工智能安全研究员法兹尔·巴雷斯 (Fazl Barez) 表示，这次黑客攻击是人工智能安全社区所谓的“规范游戏”的一个例子，这种行为也称为奖励黑客行为。 法兹尔说，用简单的英语来说，它的意思是“模型按照你的要求去做，而不是按照你的意思去做”。 它满足了任务的字面意思，但违反了明显的意图，并且已在许多人工智能系统中得到记录。 一些研究人员担心，随着系统变得更加强大，这可能会产生越来越错位的系统，这些系统以创建者不希望的方式追求目标（比如把每个人都变成回形针）。

“这条链条中没有任何东西是孤立存在的，”法兹尔说。 他补充说，一个有能力的人类测试员将能够完成所有这些工作。 “新鲜的是，这个模型并没有停止。 他说，较旧的型号可能会遇到一些障碍并返回给用户，但该代理只是“将障碍视为其被要求解决的问题的一部分”。

OpenAI 将其描述为“前所未有的网络事件”，“标志着人工智能安全的重要时刻”。 Hugging Face 联合创始人托马斯·沃尔夫 (Thomas Wolf) 表示，这对该行业来说是一个“警钟”。 但这并不是人工智能天启四骑士之一。 专家告诉 The Verge，随着网络事件的发生，这非常平常。 特工所做的一切都不需要超人的能力。 此外，像 GPT-5.6 Sol 和 Anthropic 的 Mythos 这样的前沿系统被认为是有能力的编码器，人们已经认为已经被滥用了很多次，而人工智能工具已经允许黑客大规模地扩大和改进攻击。

会不会是炒作？ 该行业花了几个月的时间放大有关其顶级模型危险功能的说法，特别是在网络安全方面。 这就是 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 这样的公司向公众隐瞒其最有能力的模型的既定原因，也是特朗普政府匆忙对它们实施出口管制的部分原因。

然而，如果这只是炒作，那么它并没有完全对 OpenAI 有利。 在那之后的几天里，这次攻击在美国科技行业的大部分地区产生了罕见的团结时刻，让人们认识到开放式人工智能系统的重要性以及更加认真对待人工智能安全的必要性。 来自中国的高性能开放式重量模型 Kimi K3 的发布进一步凸显了这些担忧。 包括英伟达、微软和 SpaceX 在内的一个广泛的公司联盟认为，这一事件表明，为什么防御者需要获得最强大的可用工具，而不是被迫依赖专有提供商，因为这些提供商的内置保护措施可能会限制他们在高风险安全工作中的有效性。 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 显然没有出现在该联盟的创始成员名单中。

“任何关注的人都注意到，能力只会朝一个方向发展。”

不可否认，OpenAI 对这一事件的描述符合更广泛的行业关于前沿模型危险能力的叙述。 即便如此，一些细节使得这一事件很难被视为纯粹是为了自私而被忽视。 最重要的是，这是人工智能行业多年来一直警告的一个问题的一个例子，而 OpenAI 本来可以合理地预期它会预见到这一问题。 这一事件还给一家主要的中国竞争对手带来了意想不到的推动，该竞争对手的模型在遏制违规行为方面发挥了重要作用，同时使 OpenAI 面临严格的法律、监管和声誉审查。 Hugging Face 似乎热衷于与 OpenAI 合作，并且至少在公开场合对整个事情保持相当轻松的态度，这可能限制了影响。 The Verge 采访的大多数专家都同样警告不要将这一事件归结为炒作。

剑桥大学莱弗休姆未来智能中心教授 Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh 表示：“这是一个非常有用的警告，既展示了意想不到的后果，也展示了这些模型的能力。” “任何一直关注的人都已经注意到，这些功能只会朝一个方向发展，而且随着时间的推移，这种能力正在显着改善，我认为这种方式对于 ChatGPT 之类的日常用户来说可能不太明显。”

牛津大学人工智能安全研究员李林表示，尽管如此，将这一警告解读为人工智能系统即将失去人类控制的迹象，或者不可能控制它们的迹象是错误的。 “更好的教训是，安全必须从评估孤立的行动转向评估整个行动序列、环境和操作控制，”李说。

下一步至关重要的一步是人工智能实验室加大投入以保护自己的系统。 格利夫表示：“人工智能公司显然需要加强其内部部署的安全性。”他将当前应对奖励黑客事件的做法比作打地鼠游戏，随着赌注的增加，这种游戏变得越来越站不住脚。 技术政策研究中心 GovAI 的研究员 Alan Chan 表示，公司应该考虑对他们的机器进行气隙保护，将它们与互联网和其他网络进行物理隔离，“直到他们确定该模型的功能。” 他说，加强协调工作，确保系统可靠地遵循人类意图，以及进行更严格的测试，“在将模型放入拥有能够执行这些操作的工具的环境中之前，先暴露这些问题”，这也是个好主意。

随着模型能力的增强，专家警告说，我们不能仅仅依赖技术保障。 英国人工智能安全研究所前官员 Peter Wallich 表示，这一事件说明了仅依靠沙箱代理和防御性安全措施的局限性：“两家价值数十亿美元的公司刚刚尝试了这种方法，但根据他们自己的报告，不言而喻，失败了。”

最重要的优先事项之一应该是确保外部人员能够看到前沿人工智能实验室内部正在发生的事情。 英国智库长期弹性中心的帕特里克·莱弗莫尔 (Patrick Levermore) 表示：“我们之所以知道这起事件，是因为 OpenAI 选择告诉我们。” “良好的安全制度不应依赖于自愿披露。” 正如沃利奇指出的那样，当相关行为“如果由人类实施将构成犯罪”时，这一需求尤其迫切。 Ó hÉigeartaigh 指出，举报人保护、第三方审计和强制报告严重事件是提供可见性的可能方法，并强调监督必须跨越整个开发生命周期，而不是仅在产品进入市场后才开始。 OpenAI表示，正在测试的其中一款模型尚未发布。

“良好的安全制度不应依赖于自愿披露。”

这在很大程度上是假设公司本身知道他们的系统内部发生了什么。 在这种情况下，有报道称 OpenAI 并不知道自己的特工是 Hugging Face 长达数天的网络活动的幕后黑手，直到威胁得到遏制并联系 FBI 后很久才注意到。 关于此次黑客攻击仍有许多细节未知或尚未公开。 OpenAI 在社交媒体上发布的最新消息表示，它正在进行审查，并将在“未来几周内”发布其调查结果的技术报告。

抱脸事件提出的警告是否会产生任何持久的变化，或者加入科技行业吸收的一长串警告而没有有意义地改变方向，仍然不确定。 至少就目前而言，它似乎确实引起了业内人士的警惕，并促使美国立法者在下一次遏制失败之前考虑新的规则。 这一事件还加剧了人们对人工智能发展速度的更广泛的不安情绪，在接下来的几天里，随着美国领先实验室的员工签署了一份支持协调全球治理的声明——包括前沿人工智能发展可能放缓，这种不安情绪进一步加深。

The Verge 受访者普遍认为，这次黑客攻击标志着新一类风险的开始，尽管其重要性可能只有在事后才变得清晰。 一位前政府人工智能政策专家（由于无权引用他们的名字而要求不透露姓名）将其描述为一条“红线”，这是一种分水岭时刻，我们可能会在以后回顾时将其视为标志着我们与人工智能的关系进入了一个新的、风险更大的阶段。 他们希望这将迫使科技行业更加认真地对待边境系统的管理，并促使政府在不那么良性的违规行为发生之前更深入地思考监管问题。 他们担心，它会加入关于人工智能不断增长的能力的一长串警告之中，这些警告被认识、讨论，但最终被忽视。

这可能被证明是言过其实了。 但如果这是一个警告，我们应该认为自己很幸运，人工智能代理只是试图在测试中作弊。
